# Package `os`

```go
package os
```

Package os provides portable operating-system interfaces. Host-backed operations are supplied by source libraries with registered host capabilities.

## Functions

### func Chtimes

```go
func Chtimes(name string, atime time.Time, mtime time.Time) error
```

Chtimes changes the access and modification times of the named file. A zero [time.Time](time.md#type-time) value will leave the corresponding file time unchanged.

The underlying filesystem may truncate or round the values to a less precise time unit. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func Create

```go
func Create(name string) (*File, error)
```

Create creates or truncates the named file. If the file already exists, it is truncated. If the file does not exist, it is created with mode 0o666 according to the injected filesystem's permission policy. If successful, methods on the returned File can be used for I/O with mode [O\_RDWR](os.md#const-o_rdwr). The directory containing the file must already exist. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func Getenv

```go
func Getenv(key string) string
```

Getenv retrieves the value of the environment variable named by key.

### func Getwd

```go
func Getwd() (string, error)
```

Getwd returns an absolute path name corresponding to the current directory as reported by the injected filesystem.

### func LookupEnv

```go
func LookupEnv(key string) (string, bool)
```

LookupEnv retrieves the value of the environment variable named by key. An unavailable host or failed lookup is reported as a missing variable.

### func Lstat

```go
func Lstat(name string) (FileInfo, error)
```

Lstat returns a [FileInfo](os.md#type-fileinfo) describing the named file. If the file is a symbolic link, the returned FileInfo describes the symbolic link. Lstat makes no attempt to follow the link. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func Mkdir

```go
func Mkdir(name string, perm FileMode) error
```

Mkdir creates a new directory with the specified name and permission bits. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func MkdirAll

```go
func MkdirAll(name string, perm FileMode) error
```

MkdirAll creates a directory named path, along with any necessary parents, and returns nil, or else returns an error. The permission bits perm are used for all directories that MkdirAll creates. If path is already a directory, MkdirAll does nothing and returns nil.

### func Open

```go
func Open(name string) (*File, error)
```

Open opens the named file for reading. If successful, methods on the returned file can be used for reading; the associated file resource has mode [O\_RDONLY](os.md#const-o_rdonly). If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func OpenFile

```go
func OpenFile(name string, flag int, perm FileMode) (*File, error)
```

OpenFile is the generalized open call; most users will use Open or Create instead. It opens the named file with specified flag ([O\_RDONLY](os.md#const-o_rdonly) etc.). If the file does not exist, and the [O\_CREATE](os.md#const-o_create) flag is passed, it is created with mode perm; the containing directory must exist. If successful, methods on the returned File can be used for I/O. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func ReadDir

```go
func ReadDir(name string) ([]DirEntry, error)
```

ReadDir reads the named directory, returning all its directory entries sorted by filename. If an error occurs reading the directory, ReadDir returns the entries it was able to read before the error, along with the error.

### func ReadFile

```go
func ReadFile(name string) ([]byte, error)
```

ReadFile reads the named file and returns the contents. A successful call returns err == nil, not err == EOF. Because ReadFile reads the whole file, it does not treat an EOF from Read as an error to be reported.

### func Readlink

```go
func Readlink(name string) (string, error)
```

Readlink returns the destination of the named symbolic link. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

If the link destination is relative, Readlink returns the relative path without resolving it to an absolute one.

### func Remove

```go
func Remove(name string) error
```

Remove removes the named file or (empty) directory. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func RemoveAll

```go
func RemoveAll(name string) error
```

RemoveAll removes path and any children it contains. It removes everything it can but returns the first error it encounters. If the path does not exist, RemoveAll returns nil (no error). If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func Rename

```go
func Rename(oldName string, newName string) error
```

Rename renames (moves) oldpath to newpath. If newpath already exists and is not a directory, Rename replaces it. If newpath already exists and is a directory, Rename returns an error. Backend-specific restrictions and atomicity guarantees are defined by the injected filesystem. If there is an error, it will be of type \*LinkError.

### func Stat

```go
func Stat(name string) (FileInfo, error)
```

Stat returns a [FileInfo](os.md#type-fileinfo) describing the named file. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

### func UserCacheDir

```go
func UserCacheDir() (string, error)
```

UserCacheDir returns the default root directory to use for user-specific cached data. Users should create their own application-specific subdirectory within this one and use that.

The injected filesystem defines how the location is selected. UserCacheDir returns an error when that backend cannot determine a location.

### func WriteFile

```go
func WriteFile(name string, data []byte, perm FileMode) error
```

WriteFile writes data to the named file, creating it if necessary. If the file does not exist, WriteFile creates it with permissions perm; otherwise WriteFile truncates it before writing, without changing permissions. Since WriteFile requires multiple system calls to complete, a failure mid-operation can leave the file in a partially written state.

## Types

### type DirEntry

```go
type DirEntry = fs.DirEntry
```

A DirEntry is an entry read from a directory.

### type File

```go
type File struct { ... }
```

File represents an open file provided by the injected filesystem.

The methods of File are safe for concurrent use.

#### func File.Close

```go
func (file *File) Close() error
```

Close closes the [File](os.md#type-file), rendering it unusable for I/O. Close will return an error if it has already been called.

#### func File.Name

```go
func (file *File) Name() string
```

Name returns the name of the file as presented to Open.

It is safe to call Name after \[Close].

#### func File.Read

```go
func (file *File) Read(buffer []byte) (int, error)
```

Read reads up to len(b) bytes from the File and stores them in b. It returns the number of bytes read and any error encountered. At end of file, Read returns 0, io.EOF.

#### func File.ReadAt

```go
func (file *File) ReadAt(buffer []byte, offset int64) (int, error)
```

ReadAt reads len(b) bytes from the File starting at byte offset off. It returns the number of bytes read and the error, if any. ReadAt always returns a non-nil error when n \< len(b). At end of file, that error is io.EOF.

#### func File.ReadDir

```go
func (file *File) ReadDir(count int) ([]DirEntry, error)
```

ReadDir reads the contents of the directory associated with the file f and returns a slice of [DirEntry](os.md#type-direntry) values in directory order. Subsequent calls on the same file will yield later DirEntry records in the directory.

If n > 0, ReadDir returns at most n DirEntry records. In this case, if ReadDir returns an empty slice, it will return an error explaining why. At the end of a directory, the error is [io.EOF](io.md#var-eof).

If n \<= 0, ReadDir returns all the DirEntry records remaining in the directory. When it succeeds, it returns a nil error (not io.EOF).

#### func File.Seek

```go
func (file *File) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error)
```

Seek sets the offset for the next Read or Write on file to offset, interpreted according to whence: 0 means relative to the origin of the file, 1 means relative to the current offset, and 2 means relative to the end. It returns the new offset and an error, if any. The behavior of Seek on a file opened with [O\_APPEND](os.md#const-o_append) is not specified.

#### func File.Stat

```go
func (file *File) Stat() (FileInfo, error)
```

Stat returns the [FileInfo](os.md#type-fileinfo) structure describing file. If there is an error, it will be of type [\*PathError](os.md#type-patherror).

#### func File.Write

```go
func (file *File) Write(data []byte) (int, error)
```

Write writes len(b) bytes from b to the File. It returns the number of bytes written and an error, if any. Write returns a non-nil error when n != len(b).

#### func File.WriteAt

```go
func (file *File) WriteAt(data []byte, offset int64) (int, error)
```

WriteAt writes len(b) bytes to the File starting at byte offset off. It returns the number of bytes written and an error, if any. WriteAt returns a non-nil error when n != len(b).

If file was opened with the [O\_APPEND](os.md#const-o_append) flag, WriteAt returns an error.

#### func File.WriteString

```go
func (file *File) WriteString(value string) (int, error)
```

WriteString is like Write, but writes the contents of string s rather than a slice of bytes.
